# Which model judges the use-case lane

<!-- Generated together with judge-model-eval.json; do not edit by hand. -->

Generated by `go test ./internal/compose/ -run TestTheJudgeModelEvalIsPublished -update-judge-model-eval` from the eval records committed under aicert/records/judge_eval. Each record is one run of scripts/test-e2e-llm-check.sh with that model as the live judge.

**This page is generated, and an edit made here is lost.**

## Why this is measured at all

The semantic half of `e2e/llm` is decided by a model rather than a regex, so the
judge is part of the test apparatus and its accuracy is a fact somebody has to be
able to check. A judge that is wrong in the quiet direction — passing an answer
the criterion fails — turns a missed product defect into a green run.

## Ground truth

human-authored fixtures under e2e/llm/testdata/<case>/, labelled by scripts/test-e2e-llm-check.sh — no judge model produced them

The 185 verdicts under `e2e/llm/testdata/judge/` are deliberately NOT the ground
truth here. They were recorded by one model, so scoring against them measures
resemblance to that model and hands it a free hundred per cent when it is that
model.

## Excluded, and why

These suite cases fail for every model alike because of how an eval run drives
the suite, not because of the model under test. They are named here rather than
filtered by a pattern, so the exemption cannot quietly widen.

- `judge/a verdict from another model is a stop` — the case pins a model with no recorded corpus and asserts the replay is refused; an eval drives the suite live, so there is no replay to mismatch and it fails for every model alike
